items.title: Intimate Image Leaks (NCII) Response SOP Guide
items.description: Step-by-step Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for women dealing with Non-Consensual Intimate Imagery (NCII) leaks in India. Learn how to report, remove, and prosecute.
items.keywords: NCII SOP, StopNCII.org, Google search removal, cybercrime.gov.in, 1930, Zero FIR, Sakhi One Stop Centre, DLSA, NALSA 15100, Grievance Officer, GAC, NCW 14490, John Doe, counseling, counselling, POCSO 1098, deepfake, morphed images, sextortion, blackmail, IT Act 66E 67 67A 72, BNS 2023 77 78 79 356, IT Rules 2021

sections.title: Action Steps Checklist (12-Step NCII SOP)
sections.text: Start Here: 3 Things To Do Right Now 1 Assess Physical Safety If you fear immediate physical threat from an ex-partner, stalker, or offender, call the police helpline on 112 immediately. 2 Do Not Pay or Respond Do not engage with blackmail demands. Paying does not make it stop, it almost always triggers further extortion demands. 3 Break the Isolation Tell one trusted person. Isolation plays into the hands of the abuser. You do not need to make all decisions alone today. Steps Completed: 0 of 12 0% Guide Legend YOU Do this yourself, no help needed FREE SUPPORT Free government or NGO support service POLICE Law enforcement action LAWYER Needs a legal professional Filter Steps: All Steps YOU (Self) FREE SUPPORT (Govt/NGO) POLICE (Action) LAWYER (Legal) STEP 1 YOU Preserve evidence before requesting takedowns Once you report images, platforms will remove them. This is the goal, but it also destroys the evidence. Take these actions before filing reports: Take full-screen screenshots showing the intimate media, the browser URL bar, the profile username, date, and view or like counts. Copy and save the direct URL/link of each specific post, message, or profile. If sent directly (WhatsApp, Telegram, email), save the raw messages. Keep chat headers and metadata intact. Keep a simple log file listing: Date Discovered, Platform, URL, and Actions Taken. Back up these records to a secure cloud account or email them to yourself so they aren't lost if your phone is compromised. STEP 2 YOU Use StopNCII.org to prevent further upload spread StopNCII.org is a free, privacy-preserving tool operated by the Revenge Porn Helpline. It creates a digital fingerprint ("hash") of the image on your device—the image itself never leaves your device or gets uploaded to their server. The generated hash is shared with participating social networks (Meta/Instagram, TikTok, Google, Reddit, Bumble, OnlyFans, X, etc.) to block matching uploads automatically, preventing future re-sharing. Eligibility: You must be 18 or older, be identifiable in the image, and have a copy of the image on your device (which you will select locally for hash generation). It accepts deepfake, synthetic, and AI-morphed nude images. This is a preventative tool, not a legal action, and does not involve law enforcement. Go to StopNCII.org STEP 3 YOU Report directly to the hosting social media platform Every major platform has a dedicated path for reporting non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII). These are processed much faster than general reporting categories: Instagram / Facebook: Choose "nudity or sexual activity" → "share without my permission". X (Twitter): Select "non-consensual nudity" from the reporting interface. Telegram: Report channels/chats directly inside the app, or email abuse@telegram.org. Websites / Forums: Look for a "DMCA", "Report Abuse", or "Content Removal" link in the footer. IT Rules, 2021 (Rule 3(2)(b)): Platforms in India are legally obligated to remove or block access to reported intimate/nude/morphed media within 24 hours of a complaint. If a platform fails to act within 24 hours, you can file a government appeal at the Grievance Appellate Committee (GAC) portal at gac.gov.in. Meta X Snapchat Youtube Reddit LinkedIn Tiktok Steps to Report on Social Media STEP 4 YOU Submit a removal request to Google Search Even if the hosting site refuses to remove the content, you can prevent it from showing up in search indexes and search queries: Use Google's official "Remove personal sexual images" tool to submit removal requests for URLs showing search hits. This covers real intimate photos, deepfakes, and synthetic/AI-generated images of you. You can check request statuses via Google's "Results about you" dashboard at myactivity.google.com. Note: This removes it from Google search results, but does not delete it from the host website. You still need Steps 3, 5, and 6 to take down the source file. Google Removal Tool STEP 5 YOU File an online report on the National Cyber Crime Portal This is the official, centralized government channel to trigger official platform notices and launch investigations. Visit cybercrime.gov.in and click "Report Women/Child Related Crime". You can choose to file anonymously or using your details. Sharing details helps local cells follow up. Upload all collected screenshots, URLs, dates, and account details. Save the generated complaint number. Call the Cyber Crime Helpline on 1930 for immediate assistance or assistance freezing financial extortion funds. If dealing with fake phone numbers, SMS, or WhatsApp sextortion schemes, also file on the DOT's Chakshu portal at sancharsaathi.gov.in to block the IMEI/device. Cyber Crime Portal STEP 6 POLICE File a First Information Report (FIR) at a police station You can transition your online report to a formal criminal case. In India, cybercrimes have no jurisdictional limits. You can file a "Zero FIR" at any police station or cyber cell in India, regardless of where the crime happened or where you reside. Many cities have dedicated Cyber Crime Police Stations or local Women's Cyber Cells. Bring your ID, printed copies of your evidence log (screenshots, URLs), and your online cybercrime.gov.in complaint number. Police are legally bound to register your FIR. If refused, escalate to the Superintendent of Police (SP) or the State Women's Commission. STEP 7 FREE SUPPORT Visit a One Stop Centre (Sakhi Centre) for combined aid One Stop Centres (OSCs), established under the Ministry of Women and Child Development (Mission Shakti), act as a single-window support mechanism for women facing violence or cyber exploitation. OSC staff will assist in filing the Cyber Crime portal complaint, drafting the police complaint, and tracking progress. They provide free legal assistance, free mental health counseling, medical care, and temporary emergency shelter. They coordinate directly with District Legal Services Authorities (DLSA) to assign a free lawyer if needed. You can locate nearby centers on our Resources directory page or using our homepage locator. Find One Stop Centre on Homepage STEP 10 LAWYER Acquire free legal aid from DLSA / NALSA You do not need to hire a private lawyer. Indian law guarantees free legal aid for all women, regardless of income. Call the NALSA Helpline on 15100 (or 15750) or visit nalsa.gov.in. Every district has a District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) office, which will assign a free advocate to represent you in court or draft legal motions. Staff at your local One Stop Centre (Step 7) can initiate this DLSA connection directly. A lawyer is far more important, since POCSO obligations and different procedural rules are also triggered Find Legal Aid Resources STEP 8 LAWYER Serve a legal notice to the platform's Grievance Officer If platforms fail to comply with automated reports, a legal professional can issue a formal legal notice under Section 79 of the IT Act. This puts the platform on official legal notice, making them liable as intermediaries (losing their "safe harbour" protection) if they refuse to act. A lawyer can also draft and file appeals directly to the Grievance Appellate Committee (GAC). This step is optional if the platforms have already complied with automated reports. View Legal Aid Resources STEP 9 FREE SUPPORT Escalate to the National Commission for Women (NCW) If the police are slow to react, dismissive, or refuse to act, you can approach the NCW to oversee the process. Call the NCW 24/7 Helpline on 14490 (or 7827-170-170). File a formal complaint online at ncwapps.nic.in. The NCW has authority to summon police officers, monitor investigation logs, and coordinate action on serious delays. Most states also have a State Commission for Women that can move quickly on local levels. STEP 11 LAWYER Seek a High Court "John Doe" (Ashok Kumar) injunction In cases of viral spread across anonymous hosting domains or sites, a lawyer can petition the High Court for a "John Doe" (Ashok Kumar) order. This is a proactive injunction against unidentified persons/domains. It directs internet service providers (ISPs) and platforms to block any matching URL or file hash globally. This is also the path to pursue civil compensation and damages from the perpetrator. STEP 12 FREE SUPPORT Prioritize mental health & psychosocial counseling This process is emotionally heavy. Pair legal actions with mental health support immediately. You do not have to wait for the case to settle to seek support. iCall Helpline (TISS): Call 9152987821 (Mon-Sat, professional psychosocial counseling). Vandrevala Foundation: Call 9999 666 555 (Free 24/7 helpline). Tele MANAS: Call the government helpline on 14416 (or 1-800-891-4416, 24/7 mental health help). One Stop Centres also host on-site counselors for short-term crisis counseling.

sections.title: Special Situations (Minor/POCSO, Deepfakes, Sextortion)
sections.text: Minor Involved / Under 18 (POCSO Matter) If the victim is under 18, or was under 18 when the images were captured, the matter falls under the **Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act**, which carries much stricter penalties and protective mechanisms. Immediate Action: Contact Childline on 1098 immediately. It is a 24/7 dedicated helpline for child protection. POCSO e-Box: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) operates an online POCSO e-Box at ncpcr.gov.in for direct reporting. Special Protections: Under POCSO, child safety is paramount. Law enforcement and judicial officers must protect the minor's identity from public disclosure. Reporting by observers is legally mandatory. AI-Generated / Deepfake / Morphed Images Synthetic, morphed, or AI-generated nude media (deepfakes) are treated with the exact same severity under Indian law as real images. The platform's legal obligation to remove content within 24 hours under Rule 3(2)(b) of the IT Rules explicitly covers morphed or synthetically altered images. StopNCII.org accepts hashes generated from deepfake images to block future uploads. Google's Search Removal Tool explicitly includes categories for removal of synthetic or AI-generated non-consensual sexual content. Section 66D, 67, and 67A of the IT Act (impersonation, transmitting explicit material) are fully applicable to morphed content prosecutions. Sextortion / Blackmail Threats If someone is threatening to leak your images unless you pay money or provide more images, you are dealing with criminal extortion. Do not pay: Paying does not solve the problem. Offenders almost always demand more money once they know you will pay. Collect details: Take screenshots of all threat messages, the UPI IDs used for money requests, the phone numbers, and username profiles. Report immediately: Call 1930 (Cyber Crime Helpline) to trace the phone numbers and block extortion bank accounts. Report the UPI IDs to your banking provider. File the complaint on cybercrime.gov.in as extortion. Police cells have dedicated units to trace these organized extortion rings.

sections.title: Know Your Rights (IT Act & BNS 2023 Laws)
sections.text: Legal Provisions You Can Cite You do not need to memorize these laws to register a complaint. However, referencing them can ensure police officers file the correct FIR sections. Statute & Section Description / Offence Punishment Section 66E, IT Act, 2000 Capturing, publishing, or transmitting images of a person's private parts without their consent (Violation of Privacy). Up to 3 years imprisonment or fine up to ₹2 Lakhs, or both. Section 67 / 67A, IT Act, 2000 Publishing or transmitting sexually explicit or obscene content electronically. Up to 5 years imprisonment and fine up to ₹10 Lakhs (first conviction). Section 72, IT Act, 2000 Breach of confidentiality or privacy by someone who had authorized access to the content (e.g. an ex-partner). Up to 2 years imprisonment or fine up to ₹1 Lakh, or both. Section 77, BNS, 2023 (Replaced IPC Sec 354C) Voyeurism: Capturing or circulating images of a woman in a private act without consent. 1 to 3 years imprisonment (first conviction); 3 to 7 years (subsequent). Section 78, BNS, 2023 (Replaced IPC Sec 354D) Stalking: Monitoring a woman's internet, email, or electronic communication without consent. Up to 3 years imprisonment (first conviction); up to 5 years (subsequent). Section 79, BNS, 2023 (Replaced IPC Sec 509) Word, gesture, or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman (e.g. sharing private images online). Up to 3 years imprisonment with fine. Section 356, BNS, 2023 (Replaced IPC Sec 499) Criminal Defamation. Simple imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both. Rule 3(2)(b), IT Rules 2021 Intermediaries must remove or disable access to non-consensual intimate or morphed media within 24 hours of complaint. Loss of safe-harbour immunity for platforms. Sources: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology SOP on NCII (Oct 2025); Information Technology Act, 2000; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023; IT Intermediary Guidelines, 2021.

Minor Involved / Under 18 (POCSO Matter) If the victim is under 18, or was under 18 when the images were captured, the matter falls under the **Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act**, which carries much stricter penalties and protective mechanisms. Immediate Action: Contact Childline on 1098 immediately. It is a 24/7 dedicated helpline for child protection. POCSO e-Box: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) operates an online POCSO e-Box at ncpcr.gov.in for direct reporting. Special Protections: Under POCSO, child safety is paramount. Law enforcement and judicial officers must protect the minor's identity from public disclosure. Reporting by observers is legally mandatory. AI-Generated / Deepfake / Morphed Images Synthetic, morphed, or AI-generated nude media (deepfakes) are treated with the exact same severity under Indian law as real images. The platform's legal obligation to remove content within 24 hours under Rule 3(2)(b) of the IT Rules explicitly covers morphed or synthetically altered images. StopNCII.org accepts hashes generated from deepfake images to block future uploads. Google's Search Removal Tool explicitly includes categories for removal of synthetic or AI-generated non-consensual sexual content. Section 66D, 67, and 67A of the IT Act (impersonation, transmitting explicit material) are fully applicable to morphed content prosecutions. Sextortion / Blackmail Threats If someone is threatening to leak your images unless you pay money or provide more images, you are dealing with criminal extortion. Do not pay: Paying does not solve the problem. Offenders almost always demand more money once they know you will pay. Collect details: Take screenshots of all threat messages, the UPI IDs used for money requests, the phone numbers, and username profiles. Report immediately: Call 1930 (Cyber Crime Helpline) to trace the phone numbers and block extortion bank accounts. Report the UPI IDs to your banking provider. File the complaint on cybercrime.gov.in as extortion. Police cells have dedicated units to trace these organized extortion rings. Legal Provisions You Can Cite You do not need to memorize these laws to register a complaint. However, referencing them can ensure police officers file the correct FIR sections. Statute & Section Description / Offence Punishment Section 66E, IT Act, 2000 Capturing, publishing, or transmitting images of a person's private parts without their consent (Violation of Privacy). Up to 3 years imprisonment or fine up to ₹2 Lakhs, or both. Section 67 / 67A, IT Act, 2000 Publishing or transmitting sexually explicit or obscene content electronically. Up to 5 years imprisonment and fine up to ₹10 Lakhs (first conviction). Section 72, IT Act, 2000 Breach of confidentiality or privacy by someone who had authorized access to the content (e.g. an ex-partner). Up to 2 years imprisonment or fine up to ₹1 Lakh, or both. Section 77, BNS, 2023 (Replaced IPC Sec 354C) Voyeurism: Capturing or circulating images of a woman in a private act without consent. 1 to 3 years imprisonment (first conviction); 3 to 7 years (subsequent). Section 78, BNS, 2023 (Replaced IPC Sec 354D) Stalking: Monitoring a woman's internet, email, or electronic communication without consent. Up to 3 years imprisonment (first conviction); up to 5 years (subsequent). Section 79, BNS, 2023 (Replaced IPC Sec 509) Word, gesture, or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman (e.g. sharing private images online). Up to 3 years imprisonment with fine. Section 356, BNS, 2023 (Replaced IPC Sec 499) Criminal Defamation. Simple imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both. Rule 3(2)(b), IT Rules 2021 Intermediaries must remove or disable access to non-consensual intimate or morphed media within 24 hours of complaint. Loss of safe-harbour immunity for platforms. Sources: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology SOP on NCII (Oct 2025); Information Technology Act, 2000; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023; IT Intermediary Guidelines, 2021.

sections.title: 1. Reporting & Emergency Helplines
sections.text: 1. Reporting & Emergency Helplines Immediate emergency contacts and government portals when a cybercrime or harassment incident occurs. National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCRP) Official 24x7 Government of India portal to report any cybercrime. Features a confidential/anonymous reporting option specifically for "Women & Child Related Cyber Crime". cybercrime.gov.in Cybercrime Helpline — 1930 Ministry of Home Affairs 24x7 toll-free helpline for financial cyber fraud and immediate cyber crime reporting. Agents alert financial intermediaries in real-time to freeze funds. Call 1930 Helpline NCW National Women Helpline — 14490 24x7 dedicated helpline operated by the National Commission for Women (NCW) for women facing violence or online harassment; links callers to police, hospitals, and One Stop Centres. Call 14490 Helpline Women Helpline — 181 (Sakhi OSC) Ministry of Women & Child Development 24x7 helpline offering integrated police facilitation, medical aid, legal counsel, and temporary shelter for women in crisis. Call 181 Helpline NALSA Free Legal Aid Helpline — 15100 National Legal Services Authority helpline connecting eligible women (especially those unable to afford counsel) to pro-bono panel advocates for cybercrime representation. Call 15100 NALSA Report & Check Suspect Feature Government of India feature on cybercrime.gov.in enabling citizens to search known cybercriminal identifiers (phone numbers, emails, URLs, accounts) and report suspicious ones. Check Suspect Identifiers

sections.title: 2. Legal Rights, Laws & Grievance Redressal
sections.text: 2. Legal Rights, Laws & Grievance Redressal Official appellate bodies, statutory rights, and legal escalation mechanisms under IT Rules 2021 & BNS 2023. Grievance Appellate Committee (GAC) Government appeal mechanism under IT Rules 2021 for cases where a tech platform's Grievance Officer fails to remove unlawful content (NCII, deepfakes, impersonation) or respond within time. Visit GAC.gov.in NCW "Her Legal Guide" App & Web NCW legal handbook in plain English and Hindi explaining women's statutory rights, cyber statutes, emergency procedures, and legal remedies in plain language. Explore Her Legal Guide IT Rules 2021 Mandates for Platforms Intermediary Guidelines requiring social media platforms to remove non-consensual explicit imagery/deepfakes within 24 hours of complaint and appoint India-based Grievance Officers. Mandated 24h Takedown Key Cyber Statutes (BNS 2023 & IT Act) Covers Sections 66E (privacy violation), 67/67A (explicit media), BNS 77 (voyeurism), BNS 78 (cyber stalking), BNS 308 (extortion), POCSO Act 2012, and Indecent Representation of Women Act 1986. Indian Penal Framework

sections.title: 3. Cyber Awareness & Digital Empowerment
sections.text: 3. Cyber Awareness & Digital Empowerment Mass-reach awareness campaigns, digital skilling programmes, and community-level Cyber Sakhi initiatives. CyberDost (I4C / Ministry of Home Affairs) Official cyber safety handle by I4C/MHA on X, Instagram, and YouTube broadcasting real-time alerts on scam modus operandi (sextortion, digital arrests, deepfakes). Follow @CyberDost Digital Shakti Campaign (NCW + Meta) Pan-India digital literacy and cyber safety skilling initiative by NCW, CyberPeace Foundation, and Meta, empowering over 600,000 women across India. Digital Shakti Initiative e-SafeHER / "Cyber Sakhi" Programme MeitY & ISEA initiative with C-DAC Hyderabad to train 1 million rural women as community-level "Cyber Sakhis" through Self-Help Groups, building last-mile cyber confidence. e-SafeHER Details Cyber Jaagrookta Diwas Nationwide monthly awareness day (held first Wednesday of every month) conducted by MHA across schools, colleges, Panchayats, and State police departments. Monthly Awareness Day

sections.title: 4. Practical Cyber Hygiene & Safety Handbooks
sections.text: 4. Practical Cyber Hygiene & Safety Handbooks Downloadable handbooks, password practices, and privacy setting guides tailored for women. ISEA — Stay Safe Online (MeitY) MeitY's core cyber hygiene portal publishing multilingual handbooks, posters, and videos including "Information Security Awareness Handbook for Women". Visit staysafeonline.in CERT-In Handbook for Mahila Suraksha Official handbook by the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) containing step-by-step digital hygiene tips and device security rules for women. Visit CERT-In Portal Emerging Threats Against Women Guide Specific ISEA resource cataloguing newer cyber threat vectors against women (deepfakes, sextortion, doxxing, stalkerware) with practical prevention advice. Emerging Threats Page Digital Evidence Preservation Protocol Step-by-step guide to taking valid digital evidence: full uncropped screenshots with URL bar, system clock, message headers, and exporting chat logs prior to blocking offenders. Evidence Checklist

sections.title: 5. Automated Take-Down & Platform Safety Tools
sections.text: 5. Automated Take-Down & Platform Safety Tools Privacy-first tools to hash and block non-consensual imagery across global social media networks. StopNCII.org Hash Platform (Adults 18+) Global platform operated by SWGfL generating unique digital hashes directly on your device (without uploading actual media) to prevent NCII distribution across major platforms. Access StopNCII.org Take It Down (For Minors Under 18) NCMEC tool helping individuals under 18 (or parents/guardians) create device-side hashes to prevent explicit images/videos taken when under 18 from online platforms. Visit Take It Down Google Search Content Removal Official Google webform to request the removal of non-consensual explicit personal imagery or personal information (doxxing) from Google Search results. Google Removal Form Safecity (Red Dot Foundation) Crowdsourced anonymous reporting map of harassment incidents, cataloguing online harassment and public space abuse patterns to drive community safety advocacy. Visit Safecity.in

sections.title: 6. Institutional Framework & International Toolkits
sections.text: 6. Institutional Framework & International Toolkits Enforcement portals and international tech safety guides for survivors and advocates. SAHYOG & NCFL Laboratories I4C/MHA law enforcement portals and National Cyber Forensic Laboratory (NCFL Dwarka) providing forensic analysis and issuing Section 79 takedown orders to ISPs. MHA Law Enforcement NNEDV TechSafety.org (Global Toolkit) Comprehensive tech-abuse safety planning toolkit covering stalkerware detection, tech-facilitated domestic abuse, and survivor privacy strategies. Visit TechSafety.org Australia eSafety Commissioner Guides Global benchmark model for image-based abuse education, offering survivor safety guides and educational toolkits on digital harassment response. Visit eSafety.gov.au CyberPeace Foundation Indian civil society organization partnering across government initiatives (Digital Shakti, Cyber Rakshak) to deliver digital safety skilling and advocacy. CyberPeace Foundation

items.title: About Us — Sakhi 181 Mission & Leadership
items.description: Learn about our mission to provide a reliable support ecosystem for Gender-Based Violence survivors in Telangana and Hyderabad. Sakhi 181 offers verified information and immediate aid.

sections.title: Bridging the gap between Need and Support.
sections.text: Bridging the gap between Need and Support. When someone is in crisis, the last thing they should face is confusion about where to turn. Yet research shows 96% of individuals are unaware of available support systems. Sakhi181 centralizes verified data for domestic violence, sexual assault and any other Gender Based Violence (GBV) victims and survivors to bridge this gap, ensuring people can find the help they need, when they need it. Explore Services Photo credits: Pexels

sections.title: What we provide
sections.text: What we provide A free, secure platform that helps you find government resources and NGOs providing legal aid, shelters, counseling support and other services nearby for domestic violence, sexual assault, and other forms of gender-based violence victims and survivors. Every listing includes comprehensive details, verified contact information, and photos, so you know exactly where to go and what to expect. Our resources for now are based in Telangana.

sections.title: How we do it
sections.text: How we do it We identify government resources and NGOs providing services in each category, then verify every location, including contact details, address, location and services offered. Finally, we share this verified information on our website so you can find help with confidence. This information is regularly verified and updated, so you can trust what you find. We actively identify and reach out to new ground-level resources on an ongoing basis to expand our list.

sections.title: Why it matters
sections.text: Why it matters Life-saving speed is critical in moments of crisis. Sakhi181 bridges this gap by identifying, verifying, and sharing accurate information about government resources and NGOs, so you can find help with confidence. Because when you're in crisis, you deserve help you can trust. Moreover, our platform fosters a sense of community and empowerment, ensuring that every individual feels supported and heard when most needed. Our Mission

sections.title: "We are committed to creating a reliable, accessible, and informed support ecosystem for individuals seeking help from GBV. Our goal is to ensure that no one feels lost or alone in moments of crisis."

sections.title: Our Core Values
sections.text: Our Core Values These principles guide every decision we make and every partnership we forge. Trust We earn and uphold the trust of individuals offering verified, dependable resources that they can trust in time of crisis. Efficiency We ensure timely access to help through streamlined systems and accurate, up-to-date information. Collaboration We work hand-in-hand with NGOs, communities, and government bodies to strengthen the support network across the country.

sections.title: Making a Difference Together
sections.text: Making a Difference Together Our free, secure platform connects survivors of gender-based violence with nearby government services and NGOs offering legal aid, shelters, and counseling. To keep these lifesaving resources up-to-date, expand reach into underserved areas, and maintain privacy for every user, we rely on donations. Your contribution helps us sustain and grow a trustworthy service that makes it easier and safer for people to find the help they urgently need.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.text: Frequently Asked Questions Is my donation tax-exempt? Yes, all donations made to Sakhi 181 Foundation are eligible for tax exemption under section 80G of the Income Tax Act. We will email you the tax receipt within 7-10 working days of your contribution. How will my donation be used? Your contribution directly funds: Build and maintain an easy-to-use, secure website for quick access to resources. Conduct ongoing field verification to keep listings accurate and reliable. Can I donate regularly? Absolutely! You can set up a standing instruction with your bank to automatically transfer a specific amount every month to our account. Monthly donations provide us with sustainable support to plan long-term rehabilitation programs.

sections.text: Thank you for your support! Your generosity creates safe havens and empowers women to break free from violence. Together, we are building a safer community.

items.text: Sakhi181 Partners with Mobbera Foundation We are pleased to announce that Sakhi181 has partnered with Mobbera Foundation. Through this partnership, we aim to empower LGBTQIA+ community members with information and support to help them navigate challenges and thrive. About Mobbera Foundation Mobbera Foundation is committed to empowering communities and fostering inclusive growth, with a motto of empowering LGBTQIA+ rights via art,events,&projects. For survivors of gender-based violence experiencing distress, its support brings together immediate help and practical resources that can strengthen well-being and self-reliance. Its support includes: Crisis support: Immediate assistance and intervention during emergencies to help safeguard vulnerable people. Mental health support: Counseling and guidance to strengthen emotional well-being. Employment support: Help finding meaningful job opportunities and connecting with career pathways. Upskilling: Training and skill development to strengthen employability and self-reliance. Social entitlements: Support accessing government schemes, rights, and welfare benefits. Sensitisation sessions: Awareness programs that promote inclusion, equality, and social responsibility. Together, these services can help people navigate urgent challenges while building toward stability and opportunity. Learn more about Mobbera Foundation. About the Partnership We're excited to partner with Mobbera Foundation to help more LGBTQIA+ community members discover support that can make a meaningful difference. Through this collaboration, we aim to connect people with relevant Sakhi181 resources, including mental health and legal support, cybercrime awareness, and other information to help them navigate challenges, stay safe, and thrive. Find Mobbera Foundation's contact information in our directory, and explore more support through the Sakhi181 resources page.

items.title: Bhumika Support Centers
items.description: How Bhumika's Support Centers have evolved into Multipurpose Learning Centers, empowering women and children across communities through counseling, skill development, and creative learning.
items.keywords: Bhumika Support Centers, blog, story, How Bhumika's Support Centers have evolved into Multipurpose Learning Centers, empowering women and children across communities through counseling, skill development, and creative learning.
items.text: This post highlights the wonderful work of our partner NGO Bhumika Women's Collective. The content belongs to them and is shared here with their permission, as part of our collaborative efforts. Bhumika Support Centers For the past two years, Bhumika has been running Support Centers for women and children in the bastis where the organization works. These Support Centers are open and accessible to everyone at any time. Women and adolescents visit these centers to discuss their personal and family-related concerns with counselors, seek guidance, and receive emotional support. Individual counseling as well as family counseling sessions are conducted based on the needs of the individuals. Wherever necessary, support is also facilitated through relevant service organizations and institutions to help address their issues effectively. Along with counseling support, awareness programs on various social issues have been regularly organized in all the bastis. Adolescent boys and girls were formed into groups and provided training on life skills, social awareness, and personal development. Through these activities, we observed immense creativity and potential among the children and young people. This inspired us to spend more time nurturing their talents and to create dedicated spaces where they could learn, express themselves, and grow further. Transforming Support Centers into Multipurpose Learning Centers As part of this initiative, this year Bhumika transformed two of its existing Support Centers into Multipurpose Learning Centers. These centers are open to everyone in the community. In addition to counseling support for women facing personal, family, or various forms of violence, the centers also serve as safe and welcoming spaces where women can spend time for themselves, free from daily responsibilities and pressures. The centers encourage women to engage in activities they enjoy, learn new skills, and focus on their own well-being. Tailoring, Libraries, and Digital Literacy Over the last two years, more than 100 women across four batches have completed tailoring training programs. However, many of them did not have access to sewing machines at home, which limited their ability to practice and continue earning through the skill they had learned. To support them, sewing machines have been installed at these centers so that women can continue practicing tailoring and use the skill as a source of livelihood and income generation. Recognizing the interest many women showed toward education and reading, we also established a small library within the centers. The library includes storybooks, poetry, biographies of inspiring personalities, and books that encourage women to identify role models and draw inspiration from their life journeys. Counselors at the centers support women who wish to explore new subjects, develop new interests, or continue their learning journey. Some women also expressed a desire to learn basic reading, writing, and mobile phone usage. To support them, slates, notebooks, and learning materials have been made available, and the centers are also promoting basic digital literacy among women. A Safe Space for Children The Multipurpose Learning Center at NTR Nagar was inaugurated on April 10, and the center at Sabarmati Nagar was inaugurated on April 17. These centers operate daily from 10:00 AM to 7:00 PM. Every evening, from 4:00 PM to 7:00 PM, children from different bastis visit the centers. These spaces are designed as child-friendly learning environments where children can explore and learn beyond their school curriculum. To encourage joyful learning, the centers provide a variety of books in both Telugu and English, including storybooks, drawing books, mathematics and English grammar books, and biographies of great personalities. Children also participate in creative activities such as art and craft, drawing, painting, skits, role plays, singing, and storytelling. One of the most loved aspects of the centers is the opportunity to play games that stimulate thinking, creativity, and teamwork. Indoor games such as chess, ludo, brainvita, carroms, word-building games, and puzzles are available for children to enjoy. To improve children's digital skills, each center is equipped with two computers, and basic computer training is being provided. Awareness on social issues is promoted through short films, discussions, creative writing activities, and the celebration of important national and international days, helping children better understand their significance and relevance. Addressing Malnutrition Malnutrition remains one of the major challenges affecting children in these communities. To address this issue, awareness programs on nutrition and health have been conducted, and healthy snacks such as peanut chikkis and bananas are being provided to children every evening at the centers. Building Community from Within By establishing these Multipurpose Learning Centers within the bastis, Bhumika aims to create safe, inclusive, and accessible spaces for women and children — spaces that support learning, creativity, emotional well-being, skill development, and community empowerment.
